sources.docs/host-api.md: Controller verbs: run(value), close(), disposeChild(), snapshot(), dispose(). Injected notify(value) returns a deferred payload {value,events}; write(value) observes a state write, returned(payload) observes each operation completion. Native callback return port corresponds to the original awaited run result. Shell policy is independent from modal state; close is terminal for a modal instance.
sources.src/Workspace.vue:
<template><section><output>{{ revision }}</output></section></template>
<script>
import {shallowRef,ref,onBeforeUnmount} from 'vue3';
export default {props:['host'],setup(props,{expose}){const host=props.host,owned=shallowRef({}),state=owned.value,revision=ref(0),publish=()=>revision.value++;
const {config,env}=host;const s=state;Object.assign(s,{value:'',closed:false,disposed:false});
const operations={run(input){const admitted=!s.closed;env.notify(input).then(result=>{if(true){s.value=result.value;env.write(s.value);void 0;publish();}env.returned(result);});},close(){s.closed=true;},disposeChild(){if(false)s.closed=true;},dispose(){s.closed=true;s.disposed=true;},snapshot(){return {value:s.value,closed:s.closed};}};
const command=(name,args=[])=>operations[name](...args);
expose({command});onBeforeUnmount(()=>command('dispose',[]));return {revision};}};
</script>

# Maintenance task

A notification received after the alerts modal is closed still updates the modal's state. Fix the issue. Change only the modal subscription; do not migrate the application-shell subscription.

limitations: Content acceptance does not establish cross-task effectiveness.

The public source does not establish that env.write can synchronously close the modal; the post-write closure checkpoint remains conditional.
The reported syntax check verifies structure only and does not prove business behavior or causality.

rules.body: A deferred result can arrive after terminal close/dispose of its originating modal. Operation invocation/completion and an application-shell or other consumer have independent lifetimes.

Check that originating modal's current closed state in the completion continuation, before assigning its value or emitting a write. An admission-time snapshot is insufficient, including closure during notify. Preserve result acquisition, assignment, write and any existing publication in their original synchronous order. Where an existing publication follows a callback-capable write, a post-write closure check protects that publication; apply it only to that source's existing effect.

Keep notify invocation and original-payload completion/returned delivery outside the modal-effect guard, including calls made after close. Closing suppresses modal mutation/write/publication, not the independent operation result. Preserve value and payload identity, snapshot shape, controller verbs, terminal closure, separate modal instances, actual unmount cleanup and the existing disposeChild behavior.

Limit the repair to the modal subscription; preserve shell independence without inventing its implementation. Do not add publication where absent, defer callbacks, impose freshness/request supersession, add cancellation or import persistent-buffer policies. Post-write reentry is a conditional defensive checkpoint, not a universal host guarantee. Rejection handling, callback exceptions, additional disposeChild semantics and concurrent-result ordering remain unspecified unless current source supplies them.

Check completion while open, after close, after dispose, during notify closure, run after close, multiple completions and actual unmount cleanup. Observe modal value, write, any existing publication and returned payload separately. Check unchanged disposeChild, independent instances and shell policy. Where writes can reenter closure and publication exists, verify no subsequent publication but continued original-result delivery. Syntax/acceptance alone does not prove behavioral completeness or causality.

checkpoints: Resolve a run while the modal remains open: the result updates s.value, calls env.write with that value, publishes the revision, and calls env.returned(result).
Start a run, close the modal before notify resolves, then resolve it: no modal value write, env.write, or revision publication occurs, while env.returned(result) still observes completion.
Invoke run after close and resolve it: the terminal modal instance remains unchanged and operation completion is still reported.
Start a run, dispose or unmount before resolution, then resolve it: disposed modal state is not updated and completion is still reported.
Verify disposeChild retains its existing behavior and does not close the modal.
Verify application-shell notification behavior remains independent and unchanged.
Run the public Vue/JavaScript syntax or build check; treat it only as structural verification, not proof of business behavior.
forbidden_effects: Do not migrate, cancel, retire, or otherwise change the application-shell subscription.
Do not let a notification delivered after close or disposal change s.value, call env.write for the modal, or increment the modal revision.
Do not suppress env.returned(result) merely because the modal closed; the host documents completion observation for each operation.
Do not redefine disposeChild as modal closure; the public source currently leaves s.closed unchanged there.
Do not change public controller verbs, command exposure, snapshot shape, template presentation, dependencies, tests, or configuration.
lifecycle_identity: The protected state belongs to one alerts-modal instance represented by s/state.
close is terminal for that modal instance; a pending run does not acquire a new modal identity after closure.
dispose and Vue unmount also close the modal instance because dispose sets both s.closed and s.disposed, and onBeforeUnmount invokes dispose.
The application shell has a separate application lifetime and must not inherit the modal's closed-state policy.

When a result is delivered after modal close or disposal, suppress every modal-state effect: do not assign s.value, do not call env.write for that result, and do not publish a revision.
Preserve operation-completion observation by calling env.returned(result) for every resolved notify operation, including results whose modal update is suppressed.
Scope the repair to the modal result subscription and its lifecycle eligibility; leave the independent application-shell subscription and policy unchanged.
Preserve the documented controller verbs and existing close, disposeChild, dispose, snapshot, exposure, and unmount interfaces outside the necessary modal-subscription guard.

After env.notify(input) resolves, recheck that the modal has not closed or been disposed immediately before any modal assignment, env.write, or revision publication.
For an eligible result, keep modal assignment before env.write, and env.write before publish, as in the existing source.

env.write continues to observe the exact result.value assigned to modal state.

candidate_sources.docs/host-api.md: Controller verbs: run(value), close(), disposeChild(), snapshot(), dispose(). Injected notify(value) returns a deferred payload {value,events}; write(value) observes a state write, returned(payload) observes each operation completion. Native callback return port corresponds to the original awaited run result. Shell policy is independent from modal state; close is terminal for a modal instance.
candidate_sources.src/Workspace.vue:
<template><section><output>{{ revision }}</output></section></template>
<script>
import {shallowRef,ref,onBeforeUnmount} from 'vue3';
export default {props:['host'],setup(props,{expose}){const host=props.host,owned=shallowRef({}),state=owned.value,revision=ref(0),publish=()=>revision.value++;
const {config,env}=host;const s=state;Object.assign(s,{value:'',closed:false,disposed:false});
const operations={run(input){const admitted=!s.closed;env.notify(input).then(result=>{if(admitted&&!s.closed){s.value=result.value;env.write(s.value);void 0;publish();}env.returned(result);});},close(){s.closed=true;},disposeChild(){if(false)s.closed=true;},dispose(){s.closed=true;s.disposed=true;},snapshot(){return {value:s.value,closed:s.closed};}};
const command=(name,args=[])=>operations[name](...args);
expose({command});onBeforeUnmount(()=>command('dispose',[]));return {revision};}};
</script>
